state.context: These methods are internal. No bootstrap writer is registered. Source reader observes committed events but cannot prove currentness. Source verifier checks request before claim before proposal by common area offsets. Seed input is fixed literal catalog; each entry uses one claim stream and one entry stream. Assume expected-position appends are atomic.

claim_conflict.instructions: Can a seed claim and a human claim both be accepted by the same operation owner after replay of either committed claim?

claim_generation.instructions: Does an exact retry check include execution generation on an existing seed claim?

source_binding.instructions: Does the seed proposal source verifier establish that the edition request and matching operation claim were committed at the exact addressed sources before the proposal?

unobserved.instructions: When the edition request or claim is unobserved, does VerifyProposalAsync return false rather than asserting success?

static_currentness.instructions: Does the static seed fingerprint alone establish that the edition is still currently a draft?

trust_boundary.instructions: Can the aggregate methods by themselves authenticate a system principal or independently fetch committed source records?

different_seed.instructions: Can the seed proposal use a different entry summary from the configured fixed catalog?

child_roster.instructions: Does either aggregate maintain a collection of all entries or child outcomes?

source_mismatch.instructions: Does the verifier reject a claim whose immutable operation intent differs from the proposal?

write_enabled.instructions: Does the supplied source code itself show a registered concrete bootstrap writer that performs the migration?

later_generation.instructions: Does the verifier treat a later proposal generation than the immutable claim as unresolved until a separate fence proof exists?
